newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to cut state jobs, but slowly.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to cut state jobs, but slowly.

text.p: Venezuela hopes to cut some 30,000 jobs from its bloated state payroll by the end of the year as part of a wider restructuring of the public sector, leading daily El Universal reported.

Senior Planning Ministry official Luis Supelano said lay-offs would gradually rise to 80,000 by the end of the century, with trimming first limited to ministries but later including other state organizations, the paper said.

Slimming Venezuela's grossly inefficient and 1.3 million workers-strong public sector is widely seen as a pre-requisite for raising real wages, as well as an essential step in the country's IMF-inspired economic reform program.
With Venezuela currently consumed by labor strife over wage claims, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff recently admitted the state could pay its employees better "if there were less of them"
